# Generated files and their checks

- Since G2 of step 9 (26 Nov 2026), the build runs asdlgen (cpp/tools/asdlgen.h) before the `c6502` library and writes the IR classes into the checked-in cpp/generated/ whenever an `.asdl` file or the tool is newer than its stamp. A change to the generator is therefore checked before any full build, or a wrong generator overwrites the checked-in files: build the tool alone with `cmake --build cpp/build --config Release --target asdlgen`, which takes seconds, and run `cpp/build/bin/asdlgen.exe --check cpp/generated c99.asdl tac.asdl asm.asdl asm2.asdl`. After an `.asdl` edit, the files a build rewrote are committed with the edit, and `git status` shows them.
- The runtime helpers are built in C++ (cpp/src/rtlib/helpers.cpp), and cpp/tests/frozen/rtlib_helpers.txt is the dump Python's rtlib/helpers.py gave. A change to a helper fails test_rtlib_helpers.cpp until the capture is written again with `cpp/build/bin/c6502cpp.exe helper-dump > cpp/tests/frozen/rtlib_helpers.txt`, which writes LF since `write_stdout` sets binary mode, and the footprints in that test change with it.
- `eol.py` of the exact-edits skill fails with a CalledProcessError once a new file is staged (added, or moved with `git mv`), since it runs `git show HEAD:<path>` for it, and it handles the file while it is untracked. Run it before `git add`, or compare `git diff --cached --numstat` with `git diff --cached --numstat --ignore-cr-at-eol` and check the new file with `eol.py --style`.
- Python reads the helpers from c6502cpp (`cpp_backend.helper_program`, `helper_footprints`), so a test that needs them runs only with c6502cpp built, like every other test that compiles.

Related: [[codebase/checks-after-python]], [[codebase/msbuild-stale-builds]], [[codebase/git-bash-on-windows]]
